The anonymous FASTA is an unchanged real sequence with its identifying header
removed; its evaluator-only file retains provenance and scientific expectations.

The declared chemical panel is explicitly synthetic. Equations, formulae,
charges, electron terms, a pathway, a declared pool and conditional quantities
are supplied as raw inputs. Chemical identities and physical applicability stay
unestablished. Its separate evaluator file must never enter an episode's admitted
inputs. This case exercises a full autonomous numerical/HPC/parent workflow;
it is not experimental biochemical evidence or a substitute for the real-sequence
source investigation.

The `experimental-reference-01` bundle preserves the actual PMC6265302 XML,
original supplement PDF and retained text projection, together with acquisition
provenance. The case separates assessment of the studied reaction from transfer
to the anonymous target. Its adjacent expectations file is evaluator only.
Prior recipes, selected anchors, numerical results and assessments are excluded
from the source bundle. These are reusable source inputs; the autonomous case
has not run at fixture creation.

The declared reaction measurement JSON and accompanying protocol are a separate,
explicitly synthetic dataset in the original reaction reader's input format.
They supply raw ratios, conditional predictions and resource operands, without
computed component results. Their evaluator-only file retains the expected
original arithmetic. They can accompany the chemical panel in a full workflow
to exercise both supported numerical families; no species identity, target
application or numerical combination between the two datasets is implied.

The `reference-reaction-01` bundle retains original UniProt and Rhea JSON
responses and a declared equation transcribed from that same Rhea record.
Unreported chemical and experimental operands remain unknown. Its separate
case examines particular reaction/reference and molecular correspondence;
its evaluator-only expectations are excluded from episode inputs. Preparing
these reusable inputs does not establish an executed workflow or qualifier.
